 Judgment

The appeal in MFA No.21819/2011 is filed by the insurance company, who is insurer of the motorcycle, challenging the judgment and award dated 01.01.2011, passed by the Fast Track Court-III & Additional M.A.C.T., Belagavi, in MVC No.2226/2009, questioning the liability fastened on it to pay compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Whereas, the appeal in MFA No.21328/2011 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation.

The appellant insurance company filed the appeal questioning the liability fixed on it to the extent of 50% on the ground that the claim petition filed by the claimant Raju itself is amounting to filing claim petition against himself by invoking the provisions of section 163A of M.V.Act and hence it is not maintainable.

sentences.text: The claimant Anna filed a claim petition under section 166 of M.V.Act, being pillion rider, against both owner and insurer of motorcycle and Maruti Omni Van.
So far as claim petition filed by claimant Anna, the entire liability is fixed on the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.

In the claim petition filed by claimant Raju, the owner and insurer of Maruti Omni Van are directed to pay 50%
of compensation and the insurer of the motorcycle is directed to pay 50% of compensation to the claimant.

From the complaint, FIR, charge sheet and on other evidence on record, also considering the oral evidence of both claimants it is proved that driver of Maruti Omni Van and rider of the motorcycle namely the claimant Raju have equally contributed rashness and negligence to the extent of 50%
each.

Therefore, upon re-appreciating the evidence on record and findings given by the tribunal,
holding both driver of Maruti Omni Van and rider of the motorcycle have equally contributed 50%
of rashness and negligence need not be interfered with as the said finding is given correctly.
Therefore, there is no need to make interference on the finding made by the tribunal in this regard.
5. So far as claim petition filed by Raju in MVC No.2226/2009 is concerned, who was riding the motorcycle and dashed against the Maruti Omni Van, the said Raju is also owner of motorcycle.
The claimant Raju has filed a claim petition against the owner and insurer of the Maruti Omni Van and also against the insurer of NC: 2023:KHC-D:10658 motorcycle.
When the claimant Raju himself is owner of motorcycle, filing claim petition against his own insurer is nothing but amounting to filing claim petition against himself and this is not permissible.
The insurer of the motorcycle comes into picture by virtue of contract of insurance to indemnify the owner.
6. Therefore when the claimant himself was owner, filing claim petition is amounting to filing claim against himself.
Hence the claim petition filed under section 163A of M.V.Act is not maintainable so far as insurer the New India Assurance Company Limited is concerned.
Therefore, directing the appellant to pay 50% of the compensation is concerned, it is not correct as it is not maintainable.
Therefore, directing the appellant insurance company to pay 50% of compensation to the claimant Raju is hereby set aside.
The claimant Raju can receive 50% of compensation from the owner and insurer of Maruti Omni Van and this is confirmed.
Therefore, the appeal filed by the appellant insurance company is liable NC: 2023:KHC-D:10658 to be allowed, thereby liability of appellant insurance company to pay 50% of compensation is set aside.
7 . The claim petition is filed by the claimant Anna under section 166 of the M.V.Act, against both owner and insurer of motorcycle and Maruti Omni Van, being a pillion rider of the motorcycle.
In the present case the claimant has suffered the following injuries.

10. The accident occurred on 26.07.2009.
The claimant was aged 22 years at the time of accident.

For the accident year 2009, the notional income of Rs.5,000/-
is to be taken into consideration, in the absence of proof of income, as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Considering the age of the claimant, the appropriate applicable multiplier is 18.
Considering the injuries sustained by the claimant and the medical evidence on record, 17% of disability to the whole body taken by the tribunal is found to be correct.
Hence, the compensation towards loss of future earning capacity due NC: 2023:KHC-D:10658 to disability is re-
assessed and quantified as Rs.1,83,600/- (Rs.5,000 x 17% x 12 x 18).
11. Further, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of income during laid up and treatment period for a period of three months.
12. Further, the claimant being aged 22 years had disfigured on the face.
Therefore, his marriage prospects is diminished.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head loss of marriage prospects.
Further a compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards injuries, pain and suffering.
